Theorem
[Existence of $k$-rarefaction waves] ↗ def:genuinely-nonlinear-linearly-degenerate ↗ def:rarefaction-curve ↗ thm:riemann-problem-solution 1. ch11:11.2-thm-1\group Conservation Laws

Suppose that for some $k\in \{ 1,\ldots ,m\} $,

(i) the pair $(\lambda _k, r_k)$ is genuinely nonlinear, and

(ii) $u_r \in R_k^+(u_l)$.

Then there exists a continuous integral solution $\mathbf{u}$ of Riemann's problem (1), (2), which is a $k$-simple wave constant along lines through the origin.

Proof

\sketch Parameterize the rarefaction curve by $u_l=\mathbf v(w_l)$ and $u_r=\mathbf v(w_r)$. Since $F_k''(s)=D\lambda _k(\mathbf v(s))\cdot r_k(\mathbf v(s))$, genuine nonlinearity and $u_r\in R_k^+(u_l)$ make $F_k$ strictly convex when $w_l<w_r$ and strictly concave when $w_l>w_r$. The scalar Riemann problem (7) with states $w_l,w_r$ therefore has a continuous centered rarefaction solution $w(x/t)$. Composing with $\mathbf v$ gives the required continuous integral solution of (1)–(2).

□
